THE MOUNTAIN SYNDICATE

By: Busisiwe Gumede | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
rchestrated by a mysterious and elusive figure known only as Charley, this illegal syndicate targets vulnerable youth, manipulates desperate parents, and weaponizes sacred tradition in a high-stakes e

Unique Selling Point:
Charley and his syndicate identify or lure teenage boys and surprisingly, girls—often those in distress or from troubled homes—and transport them to a remote area under the pretense of a traditional initiation. Parents only learn their child is missing after a frantic search. Then comes the call:
“Your child is with us. He’s seen sacred rituals. If you don’t want him initiated, pay a fine—R4000 or more.”
The parents are told their child cannot leave because they are on a "waiting list," and having witnessed rituals, they must now be "cleansed" or "compensated for." It’s a chilling mix of extortion and cultural manipulation.
The Victims:
Families who refuse to pay are told their children will be harmed or "left behind" spiritually. Even when rescued, children return visibly changed—detached, secretive, and seemingly brainwashed. They claim they’ve been told they’ll go mad or die if they don’t complete the "course." Parents report that their sons begin idolizing Charley and the "brotherhood," often running away again to rejoin it.

Press Release:


Mountain Syndicate
It’s a chilling mix of extortion and manipulation. Around Soshanguve, children are disappearing into the clutches of a shadowy group allegedly posing as a traditional initiation school. For desperate parents receiving a ransom call, the group seems to be no more than a kidnapping syndicate. But why do police turn a blind eye, even when terrified parents plead for help? And why are some of the “rescued” children so detached, secretive, and desperate to return to the bush? What’s really happening inside this so-called school?
Producer: Busisiwe Gumede-Chizhanje | Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli

Script:


(Macfarlane) Each morning in Daveyton, on Joburg’s East Rand, children walk to
school. But some never return home.
(Gogo Rejoice Sibanda Subtitle) She disappeared. We searched and searched but
couldn't find her.
(Gogo Rejoice Sibanda Subtitle) They said your child has gone for initiation.
(Gogo Rejoice Sibanda Subtitle) Initiation? How?
((Gogo Rejoice Sibanda Subtitle) I didn’t know where she was. I hadn’t consented to
anything, who did she go there with?
(Macfarlane) Some were lured by promises of belonging, others by fear and threats. But
all these children are victims of an alleged syndicate that it seems no one can stop.
(Macfarlane) A girl’s life is on the line - and we’re desperate to find her. But our
investigation will take us down a dark and unexpected path.
(Macfarlane Subtitle) Go guys! We’re not going to be sitting in the middle of nowhere.
(Camera Man Subtitle) They are giving us trouble.
(Macfarlane Subtitle) Don’t stop! Keep going, keep going.
(Camera Man Subtitle) Yes, but they are here, eish!
(Macfarlane) In April, a 17-year-old girl we’ll call Thembi, to protect her identity,
disappeared.
(Macfarlane) When she didn’t come home from school, her grandmother Gogo Rejoice
reported her missing with the police.
(Macfarlane) When Gogo returned home, some locals told her what had happened.
(Gogo Rejoice Sibanda Subtitle) A group of girls came here. They told me she had gone
for initiation.
(Macfarlane Subtitle) Initiation?

(Gogo Rejoice Sibanda Subtitle) Yes.
(Macfarlane) Then a group of boys arrived with a chilling letter.
(Gogo Rejoice Sibanda Subtitle) They said, since she is already inside, I would have to
pay R5000 to get her back.
(Macfarlane) Who had taken Thembi? Gogo’s only clue: a number for a man called
Charlie.
(Macfarlane) We’ve spoken to several people who, like Gogo, have lost children to so-
called initiation schools… and received ransom demands in turn for their release.

(Macfarlane) It seems to be a sinister new trend across the country.

(Lucky Magetla) The intention here is not to uphold, you know, our culture. It's about
making money.

(Macfarlane) Lucky Madigetla is a member of the Daveyton Community Policing Forum.
Last week, he was part of an operation with the police that rescued 14 children from a
suspicious initiation school on the other side of the province, near Winterveld.

(Lucky Madigetla) We had kids who say the last time I checked, I was standing in a
corner with my friends. How I got into the kombi, I don't know. I just woke up there. Now
you say to yourself, were they drugged?

(Macfarlane) The initiation offered by the schools bears no resemblance to recognised
cultural practices. And parents are charged a hefty fee.

(Lucky Madigetla) Let’s say now you've got about 30 boys and then you are expecting
three and a half thousand. Now you are demanding R3000. Then how much do you
have?

(Macfarlane) That’s over a hundred grand for just one group of initiates.

(Macfarlane) And if families refuse to pay for the so-called initiation? The dodgy schools
resort to ransom demands - turning tradition into straightforward kidnapping.

(Macfarlane) Gogo is convinced that Thembi is being held at one of these schools. In
the absence of assistance from the police, she’s come to us for help.

(Macfarlane) Charlie’s number is our only lead, and maybe our best shot at finding the
missing teen.

(Sibongile Subtitle) Hello.

(Gogo Rejoice Sibanda) Can I speak to…

(Sibongile Subtitle) The one who’s at the mountain?

(Gogo Rejoice Sibanda) Yes, I’m urgently trying to locate her. We’re ready to pay any
randsom to get her back.

(Sibongile) Okay, it’ll be R1500.

(Macfarlane) They are asking for a R1500 ransom - unashamedly and clearly, this is
how they operate.

(Macfarlane) With the terms set, we head off to Winterveld, more than 100 kilometres
away. I take over comms.

(Macfarlane) Let’s see if we can get a hold of them again.

(Macfarlane Subtitle) I want to navigate to you.

(Sibongile Subtitle) Oh, should I send you the location?

(Macfarlane Subtitle) Yes, please send the location.

(Sibongile Subtitle) To this number?

(Macfarlane Subtitle) Yes, to this number.

(Macfarlane) We don’t know if this is where the girl is or if it’s just a meeting place first
but let’s hope for the best and hopefully we can get this girl.

(Macfarlane) In the moments before meeting Sibongile, the situation is uncertain and
unnerving. Our crew, including a drone operator, is accompanied by a private security
detail.

(Macfarlane) Not wanting to scare her off and jeopardise Thembi’s rescue, it’s decided
our producer will meet Sibongile.
(Macfarlane) At the agreed meeting spot, we hand over the agreed release fee.
(Macfarlane) Then, she agrees to show us the school.
(Producer) She claims to be the one allowed to go to this place. And that's why we are
following her.
(Producer) But be very careful because it looks like they’ve got people everywhere.
(Macfarlane) It’s such a delicate thing when you’re doing these kinds of things because
one, you don’t want to lose the child. Two, you don’t want to scare these guys into not
cooperating. They
(Macfarlane ) it looks like they've found the girl.
(Macfarlane) Sibongile, where are you going? Don't run, you’re running!

(Macfarlane) They have just run away. As we have come they have just run away.
Damn it! But the girl is safe. There she is.
(Macfarlane Subtitle) Where are you from? Are you okay? Where did they take you?
(Thembi Subtitle)
(Macfarlane) You know having daughters, it's just heartbreaking to see stories like this
because I can't begin to imagine as a parent not knowing where your child is. And even
upon their return them coming back like this. It’s just, but thank God we found her.
Thank God we found her.
(Macfarlane) We’ve spoken to at least four families who - like Gogo - have had to face
syndicates like this and pay hard-earned ransoms to get their children back.
(Macfarlane) Many others can’t afford the fee and are waiting for their children to
complete the so-called initiation and return.
(Moses Dladla) If the parents are being threatened to pay this money, we encourage
them to say, come open the case. Let's investigate.
(Macfarlane) Moses Dladla is the Station Commander for Soshanguve, outside Pretoria.
(Macfarlane) Winterveld, where we found Thembi, falls under his jurisdiction.
(Macfarlane) It's mostly during the winter season in our area. As you see, we are now
stepping into winter, that's where we get these cases around us, even the escort, the
request for escort.
(MacFarlane) It seems police are happy to escort parents to rescue their children - but
there’s no official record of the disappearances.
(Moses Dladla) And once we get these kids, the parents are happy to reunite with these
kids. They don't proceed with cases whatsoever.
(Macfarlane) And without cases - how can the syndicates be stopped?
(Macfarlane) Thembi’s story isn’t over yet. Our producer’s phone rings: it’s Sibongile.

(Sibongile Subtitle) You want a statement?
(Macfarlane) We don’t want a statement. We want to speak to you.
(Macfarlane) Perhaps she feels there's nothing she has done or she wants to give us
her side of the story.
(Macfarlane) But as we approach the meeting point, things take a turn. Sibongile has
brought backup.
(Macfarlane) Sensing danger, we rush to the nearest police station.
(Macfarlane) But this syndicate doesn’t scare easily—not even with cops around.
(Police Officer Subtitle) What we are dealing with here is a serious crime.
(Sibongile Subtitle) They are the ones who filmed us without our permission.
(Police Officer Subtitle) Yes, but what you’re doing is wrong.
(Police officer Subtitle) You’re not supposed to be doing what you are doing.
(Sibongile Subtitle) Is it right that they take videos of me without my permission?
(Police Officer Subtitle) They are wrong and you are wrong too.
(Macfarlane) Despite Dlada’s insistence that there are no kidnapping cases on record,
these officers seem to know who Sibongile is.
(Police Officer Subtitle) You keep on collecting the children. I’ve got cases here that are
open from daveyton.
(Police officer 2 Subtitle) Don’t take videos.
(Producer Subtitle) We are working.
(Macfarlane) In the end, the syndicate backs off, and the police escort us out of
Winterveld. Gogo and Thembi are safe.

(Macfarlane) But there’s nothing to stop other children being lured from home.
(Macfarlane) Brigadier shouldn't a greater effort be put into this? Because when we
were there, the police knew of these cases.
(Moses Dladla) If they are reported, this case is obvious, we'll assign the detectives to
investigate, and ultimately, after the investigation, will ensure that we arrest.
(Macfarlane) Dladla insists ultimate responsibility for breaking this pattern lies with
government, notably the Department of Cooperative Governance and Traditional
Affairs.
(Macfarlane) Out of perhaps hundreds of missing teens, one has been returned to her
family. But how much did our rescue achieve?
(MacFarlane) Two weeks ago, Thembi returned to the school. She was later found and
for now, she’s home. But what happened to her on the mountain? And will she ever be free
of it?
